artifacts.summary: Root-causes the measured handoff-validation incident to a stale worked JSON example in lean-implementation-hard-agent.md (missing artifacts, stale continuation_context), recommends route (b) over (a)/(c)/(d) with evidence, and specifies a section-scoped lint-agent-contracts.sh check plus a dependency edge on Task 359.

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/core, lint-agent-contracts.sh's Check F (return-meta artifacts-template presence) is a whole-file scan: it PASSes an agent file if a correctly-shaped `artifacts` block appears ANYWHERE in the file, even if the specific section being checked (e.g. the .orchestrator-handoff.json wrap-up example, as opposed to the .return-meta.json section) is actually missing it. A whole-file-scan lint check cannot distinguish between two independent JSON-shape contracts documented in the same agent file; a section-scoped check (anchored on a nearby literal marker) is needed when a file hosts multiple independently-validated JSON shapes.

Six of the seven .orchestrator-handoff.json writer agents (general-implementation-agent, planner-agent, neovim/nix/email/lean-implementation-agent) share an identical, correct boilerplate paragraph (prose + schema pointer + explicit {type,path,summary} shape callout) instead of a literal worked JSON example. Only the *-hard family (lean-implementation-hard-agent, formerly cslib-implementation-hard-agent) embeds a full hand-maintained JSON example instead, and that is exactly where a required field (artifacts) was found dropped. When auditing a multi-writer contract for drift, check the *-hard/specialized variants first — they are the ones most likely to have forked away from the shared boilerplate that keeps the other writers correct.
